title: The Design Brief
concept: A steel bioreactor that does not exist yet is nervous about Alaska's power. The plan's second AI exists to keep living cells working as power rises and falls. The film tests that against the fair objection (no results, a controller can't make power cheaper, ship the ash to cheap power) and lands on the honest read: energy is the design brief.

fingerprint.palette: midwinter indigo dusk sky, snow-blue floor, coal black ash, galvanized steel, ember orange that means only electricity, simulation lime that means only the model
fingerprint.metaphor: a steel bioreactor with a face that flinches whenever the power gauge drops, because the plan's second AI exists to keep living cells working on Alaska's wobbling power

palette: midwinter indigo dusk, snow-blue, coal black, galvanized steel, ember electricity, simulation lime
divergence_note: A dusk exterior yard with a faced steel tank and a power gauge, cutting to a round table in the snow, a macro cell, a sample bench, a cutaway, a monitor desk, a pier with a barge and a fork in the snow. 10-08 was a dawn pier with a burning glass lens, 10-07 an overcast gravel bar with a fortune ball, 10-06 a warm stove-lit interior with a brass bell, 10-05 a seafoam school corridor. This film is cold indigo night with a single ember accent, the hero has a face and the clock is a needle.

angle.thesis: The AI in this plan isn't mainly there to find rare earths in coal waste. A second AI is there to keep living microbes working as power rises and falls, so Alaska's hardest input, energy, is the design brief and not an afterthought.
angle.falsifiable_by: If the 2030 results show the bioreactor controller ignores available energy, or the energy and cost evaluation is a footnote, the thesis is false. No results exist yet.
supporting_facts: c6 a second AI effort will adjust the bioreactor as conditions and available energy change
c7 the refinery is tested first as a virtual pilot plant, computer models
c11 Aggarwal: Alaska's remote energy challenges make energy use central
angle.fair_counterpoint: Nothing has been tested (c9), no Alaska coal source is named, UAF is one of four partners with about $913,000 of roughly $6M, and a controller can adapt to costly power but can't make power cheaper. The old answer, ship ash where power is cheap, still has to be beaten.
angle.second_movement: UAF joins, not leads: a seat at a national table, and the virtual plant is only models.
runner_ups: Planned-not-proven skeptic reading (valence curious): true but the same facts, folded in as the Act 3 test.
Waste-as-feedstock comedy: kept as a sight-gag source.
angle.cross_challenge: All three analysts converged on energy-as-design-brief. The skeptic lens was folded in as Act 3: no results, a controller can't cut the power price, ship the ash. The comedian lens supplied the WASTE to FEEDSTOCK? tag and OUTSIDE ONLY sticker.

treatment.winner: The Dramatist's structure (energy is the opponent, the barge is the test) with the Comedian's sight gags, the Enthusiast's faced SteelVessel and dashed-twin states, and the Explainer's award pie
treatment.why: All four pitches converged on a faced steel vessel and a power gauge; the Dramatist's Act 3 barge scene draws the strongest fair case against the angle at full strength, and the Enthusiast's honest narrowing keeps it celebratory but earned.

hook.frame1: A dashed ghost outline of a steel tank in a snowy indigo yard beside a round power gauge, the needle slamming into the red as the lamp dips and the ghost eyes snap open.
hook.headline: A TANK NERVOUS ABOUT POWER
hook.loopback: The last frame is the same yard, the tank back to its dashed ghost, the needle dropping again and the tank adjusting instead of flinching.

shots.title: The needle slams down
shots.centered: the ghost tank at x330 y1240
shots.means: Hook. Frame 1 is already the film: a lime-outlined model of a steel tank, only half drawn in, stands in a snowy indigo yard beside a round power gauge, and the needle SLAMS down, the yard lamp dips and the whole frame darkens. The model tank's eyes snap open and a sweat drop slides. Pencil hatch ticks fill the outline as if it is still being designed. A price tag hangs on the pole.
shots.ambient: snow falls, stars twinkle, the cable pulse crawls, the model outline crawls, the lamp flickers

hero.name: GhostTank
hero.detail_note: 60% model tank and face, 25% gauge and cable, 15% yard

shots.title: Four chairs at a round table
shots.means: A UAF NEWS card stamps down, then a round table in the snow under the lamp. Three chairs slide in first (UAA, MONTANA TECH, WYOMING) and leave a gap. The UAF chair scoots into the gap last, its JOINING tag lighting. Nobody takes a head seat because the table is round. The camera pulls back to show the whole table.
shots.ambient: snow falls, the lamp sways, steam curls from three mugs

hero.name: RoundTable
hero.detail_note: 50% chairs and cards, 30% table, 20% card and yard

shots.title: The slice
shots.means: The round table becomes the round pie. Overhead on a paper award ledger, a pie of about $6 million is drawn to true proportion and the UAF wedge, 15 percent, pulls out in paper white with a UAF pennant. Plate: UAF SHARE, ABOUT $913,000.
shots.ambient: ledger lines scroll faintly, the pie rim shines, a pen scratches a tick beside the wedge

shots.title: Waste or feedstock
shots.centered: the ash heap at x540 y1250
shots.means: Low and close at the foot of a big heap of coal refuse and ash with a WASTE tag on its stake. The tag flips to FEEDSTOCK? as tiny microbes crawl up the heap and carry specks away. Snow falls on the heap. Plate: COAL REFUSE AND ASH.
shots.ambient: snow falls, tag sways on the stake, ash dust lifts, microbes crawl

shots.title: Atoms cling outside
shots.means: Down into the macro world. One big cell, its outer wall breathing. Rare earth atoms click onto the OUTSIDE of the wall like burrs, and one atom presses in, dimples the wall and is pushed back out. Plate stays ILLUSTRATIVE throughout.
shots.ambient: the membrane breathes, atoms jitter, bokeh drifts, specks float

shots.title: Two tools, one under a tarp
shots.centered: jars at x300 y1230 and tarp at x770 y1230
shots.means: A long plank bench out in the snow under the lamp, split by a line of dashes. Left, three sample jars with a dashed search reticle hunting across them, plate AI WILL PREDICT RECOVERY. Right, a lump under a heavy tarp that bulges and lifts one corner. Plate TWO AI TOOLS PLANNED.
shots.ambient: snow falls, the reticle drifts, the tarp breathes, jar glints

shots.title: The tarp comes off
shots.means: The tarp whips off the bench lump and a governor in a dashed lime PLANNED frame spins up beside the worried tank and reaches for its valve, but the tank stays worried. The gauge needle swings wildly and the lamp pulses. Plate: AI WILL ADJUST THE BIOREACTOR. Three cells in the barrel window droop, then a sealed RESULTS envelope drops in the corner.
shots.ambient: snow falls, lamp pulses, flyballs spin, the needle swings, the cable pulse runs

shots.title: Cells stall when power does
shots.centered: the tank cutaway at x470 y1280
shots.means: A cutaway window in the tank barrel: rows of small round cells working. As the needle beside it sinks into the low zone and the whole yard darkens, the cells slow, droop and stall one by one, and the tank shivers. Plate: CAN CELLS KEEP WORKING, ILLUSTRATIVE.
shots.ambient: cells wiggle, bubbles, the needle trembles, the yard dims, snow falls

shots.title: The professor says so
shots.means: An ember pulse runs along the cable from the gauge to the tank, and the quote plate rides in on it, typed in serif with the nameplate SRIJAN AGGARWAL, UAF PROFESSOR. The tank's cell window speeds up and slows with the lamp as the pulse arrives.
shots.ambient: snow falls, the lamp flickers, the cable pulse runs, the tank breathes

shots.title: Built in software first
shots.means: A desk in a shed with a monitor. The screen boots and a lime outline of the tank draws itself with its internals, the virtual pilot plant. Plate: VIRTUAL PILOT PLANT.
shots.ambient: scanlines, the model jitters, a desk-lamp glow, snow outside the window

shots.title: No results yet
shots.means: A NO RESULTS YET stamp slams across the lime model on the screen and the model flickers and shakes.
shots.ambient: scanlines, the model flickers, dust jumps off the desk

shots.title: The price does not move
shots.means: Out in the yard at the pole. The dashed PLANNED governor nudges the gauge dial and the needle steadies, but the PRICE tag on the pole creeps down, strains, and snaps back like elastic with a clunk, and the lamp dims. Plate: IT ADAPTS and CAN'T MAKE POWER CHEAPER.
shots.ambient: snow falls, the lamp flickers, the cable pulse crawls, flyballs spin

hero.name: PriceTag
hero.detail_note: 40% pole and tag, 35% governor and gauge, 25% yard

shots.cut_reason: the stamp's thud is still ringing and the cut lands on the governor's nudge, half a second into the next line

shots.title: The obvious alternative
shots.means: The pier. A barge with a face and a deck of ash sacks slides in, mast sign SHIP IT, and its horn blows on the words ship the ash while a painted billboard sun on a post, CHEAPER POWER SOMEWHERE, rises behind it. The tank watches its own cable on the shore, sweating, its cell window dimming. Plate: THE OBVIOUS ALTERNATIVE, SHIP IT.
shots.ambient: water ripples, the barge bobs, the billboard rays turn, snow falls, the wake crawls

shots.title: The envelope opens
shots.means: The sealed RESULTS envelope opens on the desk and a card rises with a lab flask and a small pilot vessel, then COST, ENERGY, ENVIRONMENT tick one by one under TO BE EVALUATED. A calendar ribbon unrolls beside it, SEPT 2026 TO AUG 2030.
shots.ambient: dust floats in the lamp, the ribbon sways, the flask bubbles

shots.title: The design brief
shots.means: Close on the gauge. An AFTERTHOUGHT tag is swept off the pole, the plate under the dial flips from POWER to DESIGN BRIEF and an OUR READ stamp lands, then the tank plugs in its cable and the camera rises to the lit yard.
shots.ambient: needle wobble, lamp pulse, snow, the cable pulse

shots.title: Two roads
shots.means: A fork in the snow. Left, the tank with its cell window glowing as the needle wobbles but holds. Right, the barge sails off toward the billboard. On the last line the needle slams and the yard dims exactly as in frame 1, but this time the cells keep working. The question plate lands, WHICH WOULD YOU BET ON.
shots.ambient: snow falls, water ripples, needle wobbles, lamp flickers
